title: Shadow a workshop end-to-end
why_matters: Workshops are where most BAs are made or broken. Before you facilitate one, you need to have watched a good one and a bad one — and to be able to name the difference. Shadowing without participating buys you the slowest, most useful learning available to you in the first month.
steps: Ask your manager which upcoming workshop is worth shadowing this week. Aim for one with at least three stakeholders in different positions.
Sit in the back. Take notes on the facilitator, not the content: every silence, every redirect, every time they restated something to check understanding.
Write up a two-paragraph private note within four hours of the workshop ending — one paragraph of what worked, one of what you'd do differently.
Send the facilitator a brief thank-you with one specific question about a moment in the workshop. They'll remember you.
success_criteria: Two-paragraph note exists in your private file. The facilitator has had a thoughtful follow-up question from you, addressed to a specific moment in the meeting.
reflection_prompt: Pick one moment in the workshop. What would you have done differently, and what's the strongest argument against your own choice?
